items.title: Anthropic reveals rogue AI agents hate CAPTCHAs, just like you
items.summary: Come inside the mind of a bot trying to convince the internet it's human.

items.title: India’s Pocket FM doubles revenue run rate to $500M as AI powers 93% of audio content
items.summary: Pocket FM uses AI to produce 99% of its new content, helping make content production about 80 times cheaper.

items.title: Instagram’s latest feature lets you add tagged posts to your profile grid
items.summary: Instagram's newest feature lets users take posts from the Tagged tab and move it to their main profile grid instead.

items.title: Google is making it easier to switch between password managers on Android
items.summary: Google's new feature will transfer your passkeys as well.

items.title: The Boring Company raises $3B in round led by UAE
items.summary: The company said it plans to dig more than 150 kilometers of tunnels in the Middle Eastern country.

items.title: AI agents are flooding public services with new requests
items.summary: “The vast majority of cases we find are people who are entitled to claim for something, claiming for that thing,” the researcher told TechCrunch.

items.title: Bending Spoons to buy collaboration tools maker Miro for $1.36B, 90% less than its 2022 valuation
items.summary: Bending Spoons is buying Miro for $1.36 billion, a huge dip in valuation for the workplace collaboration startup, which was valued at $17.5 billion in late 2021.

items.title: Maven Robotics wants to steal your robot deployment deal
items.summary: Maven Robotics emerged from stealth today with a $100 million Series A and active deployments.

items.title: Google signs its biggest rice-methane carbon credit deal with Indian startup Mitti Labs
items.summary: The four-year agreement will cover rice farms across three Indian states, reaching about 100,000 hectares at peak delivery.

items.title: ID verification giant IDScan confirms data breach with more than 150 million driver’s licenses stolen
items.summary: The ID checking company said the data breach included people's full names and driver's licenses and other government-issued identity documents.

items.title: Snapchat takes aim at Partiful with new event-planning features
items.summary: Snapchat says the new features can be used to organize everything from birthday celebrations and sporting events to study sessions and weekend hangouts.

items.title: Defense tech Mach Industries doubles valuation to $3.7B in 3 months
items.summary: The buzzy startup raised another $600 million in a Series C extension round, bringing the total of the round to $900 million.

items.title: European founders and VCs urge lawmakers ‘to get EU Inc right’
items.summary: Amid negotiations for a new EU-wide corporate status, an open letter signed by unicorn founders and investors warns that 'EU Inc.' shouldn’t be watered down.

items.title: US Army places $11M bet on Austin-based GPS alternative Tern
items.summary: Tern has described its tech as "Google Maps for the battlefield."

items.title: AI research startup Listen Labs scrubbed a $1.5B funding round for Salesforce talks
items.summary: Listen Labs walked away from a signed Series C term sheet from Menlo Ventures, sources say.

items.title: Automattic’s board forces CEO Matt Mullenweg into leave of absence
items.summary: Mullenweg said in a company Slack message that it was against his will.

items.title: OpenAI adds a prominent AI doomer to its board of directors
items.summary: Paul Christiano, an influential AI researcher focused on alignment, is joining the OpenAI Foundation as a member of its board.

items.title: Massachusetts hits data centers with new clean power rules
items.summary: Massachusetts has become the third state in as many months to slap new restrictions on data center development.

items.title: Apple’s new CEO is reviving a Steve Jobs strategy from 25 years ago
items.summary: John Ternus made the case in his first keynote as Apple CEO that the iPhone isn't going anywhere.

items.title: Apple Watch’s new AI features are normalizing the idea that technology is always listening
items.summary: Apple says its new watches won’t save raw audio, but features that can transcribe recent speech and summarize ambient conversations raise new questions about consent, privacy, and how people behave when they know they could always be recorded.
